findings.title: Early return in Shell::ResetOnProfileEndListener skips erasing stale isolate-keyed callback map entry, leading to use-after-free
findings.message: Shell::ResetOnProfileEndListener(Isolate*) is responsible for tearing down the per-isolate profiler-end callback state before an Isolate is disposed. The function was modified to add an early 'if (options.enable_inspector) return;' guard BEFORE the call to profiler_end_callback_.erase(isolate). When the inspector is enabled, the function returns immediately without erasing the isolate's entry from the profiler_end_callback_ map (which stores v8::Global<Function>/v8::Global<Context> handles keyed by Isolate*). Callers of ResetOnProfileEndListener (e.g. SourceGroup::ExecuteInThread, Worker::ExecuteInThread, Shell::Main, Shell::QuitOnce) call this function immediately before disposing the Isolate, expecting all isolate-associated state to be cleaned up. Because the erase is skipped whenever the inspector is enabled, the stale map entry (and the dangling Isolate* key, plus Global handles bound to a soon-to-be-destroyed Isolate) survives isolate disposal. Any later interaction that touches profiler_end_callback_ with the freed Isolate pointer (e.g. HasOnProfileEndListener/TriggerOnProfileEndListener being invoked again, e.g. if the isolate address is reused or the map is iterated/looked up) results in a use-after-free, since the stored Global<Function>/Global<Context> objects reference memory owned by the disposed isolate.
findings.suggestion: Perform the profiler_end_callback_.erase(isolate) call unconditionally, before checking options.enable_inspector, so the per-isolate map entry is always cleaned up regardless of whether the inspector console (D8Console) is installed. Only the D8Console-specific cleanup (console_delegate cast and DisposeProfiler()) should be skipped when the inspector is enabled.

ground_truth.root_cause: The cleanup guard for D8Console-specific teardown (skip when inspector enabled) was placed before the unconditional map-erase operation that must always run to keep the isolate-keyed profiler_end_callback_ map in sync with isolate lifetime, causing the erase to be conditionally skipped and leaving dangling references to a disposed Isolate.
